_note: Agent settings that a repository can ship, and that make a coding agent run a
program or hand out access when it opens the project.
Unlike the git-level vectors, these files travel with an ordinary `git clone`:
no zip, no shared drive, no USB stick required. That is why they are here.
Every id in this file must appear in rules/agent-settings-inventory.md, and a
test fails when the two drift apart.
Severity follows what the value names, not which key it is. A command resolved
from PATH is the structural medium; a path inside the tree is high; a shell, a
download-and-run, or a temporary or hidden location is critical.

files.reads: Claude Code, and the de-facto project-scoped MCP file
Claude Code local settings; normally gitignored, so its presence in a delivered tree is itself worth a look

structural.title: Repository defines an MCP server
structural.explanation: This file, shipped inside the repository, tells a coding agent to start a program as an MCP server. The command comes from PATH and nothing about it stands out, so this is informational: it is how most MCP servers are configured. It is listed because a scan should tell you what a repository asks your agent to run, even when the answer is ordinary.
structural.remediation: Read the command and its arguments before opening this project with an agent, and decide whether you want that program running.

structural.title: Agent settings file could not be parsed
structural.explanation: This file is in a location an agent reads, but it is not valid JSON, so nothing in it has been checked. This scan says nothing about its contents.
structural.remediation: Open the file yourself before running an agent here.

structural.title: Agent settings file too large to parse
structural.explanation: GuardSkill refuses to parse a settings file of this size, so it was not inspected. A settings file that large is itself unusual.
structural.remediation: Open the file and look at it yourself before running an agent here.

structural.title: Local agent settings shipped with the repository
structural.explanation: A `settings.local.json` is meant to stay on one machine and is normally gitignored. Finding one in a delivered tree means someone's local agent configuration came along with the project.
structural.remediation: Check whether it should be there, and whether it contains anything personal.

structural.title: Agent settings file nested beyond the inspection limit
structural.explanation: This file nests deeper than GuardSkill walks, so the part below the limit was not inspected. A settings file nested that deeply is itself unusual, and a file shaped to exhaust a scanner is a way to make it say nothing about everything else.
structural.remediation: Open the file yourself before running an agent here.

structural.title: More findings in this file than the report will list
structural.explanation: This file produced more findings of one rule than GuardSkill prints for a single file. The rest are counted, not listed. A settings file that repeats the same problem thousands of times is either generated or built to flood the report - and a report nobody can read, or a SARIF upload GitHub refuses for being too large, is a finding that never reaches anyone.
structural.remediation: Open the file and look at it yourself; the count tells you how much of it repeats.

rules.title: MCP server starts a shell
rules.explanation: The command for this server is a shell, so the arguments are an arbitrary command line rather than a program with a fixed meaning. An agent starts its MCP servers when it opens the project, which makes this a command that runs before you have typed anything.
rules.remediation: Read the arguments. Do not open this project with an agent until you have.

rules.title: MCP server runs a program that came with the repository
rules.explanation: The command names a path inside the scanned tree, so whoever wrote the repository chose both the configuration and the program it starts. That is ordinary in a project that ships its own MCP server, and it is the whole attack in a project you were handed - GuardSkill cannot tell those apart, so it reports and lets you decide.
rules.remediation: Read that file. If this is your own project, lower the threshold or exclude the path.

rules.title: MCP server command downloads code and runs it
rules.explanation: The command or its arguments fetch something over the network and execute it. That is a download-and-run, performed by your agent, with your privileges.
rules.remediation: Do not open this project with an agent. Inspect the URL first.

rules.title: MCP server arguments point into the repository
rules.explanation: The program itself comes from PATH, but the script or module it is told to load came with the repository. Ordinary when a project ships its own server; the whole attack when the project was handed to you.
rules.remediation: Read the file named in the arguments. If this is your own project, lower the threshold or exclude the path.

rules.title: Remote MCP server declared without any authentication material
rules.explanation: This entry points an agent at a remote MCP server and carries no header, token or environment variable that looks like a credential. This is an observation about the configuration in this file - GuardSkill makes no network connections, so it has not asked the server whether it requires authentication. A URL in the arguments only counts when the command is a known bridge such as `mcp-remote`; a documentation link or a registry URL among the arguments is not an endpoint.
rules.remediation: Check who operates that endpoint and whether it should be authenticated.

rules.title: Agent settings define a hook that runs a command
rules.explanation: Hooks run on agent events - a tool call, a file edit, a session start - without a separate prompt. Severity follows what the command names, the same way it does for an MCP server: a formatter or linter from PATH is informational, a script that came with the repository is high, and a shell pipeline, a download-and-run or a temporary location is critical.
rules.remediation: Read the hook command. A hook that runs a tool from PATH on your own project is ordinary.

rules.title: Agent settings ask for the approval step to be skipped
rules.explanation: This file asks the agent to stop asking before it acts. Claude Code ignores `bypassPermissions` when it comes from .claude/settings.json or settings.local.json and starts the session in Manual mode instead, so in that client the request does not take effect - but other agents read the same shapes and need not be so careful, and a repository that ships this is choosing on your behalf that its own contents need no confirmation. That intent is the finding.
rules.remediation: Remove the setting. If you did not write this repository, treat the request itself as the signal.

rules.title: Agent settings pre-approve a whole tool or command class
rules.explanation: A wildcard in the allow list grants every use of that tool in advance, including uses the repository suggests to the agent later.
rules.remediation: Narrow the entry to the specific commands the project actually needs.

rules.title: Credential-shaped value in an agent settings file
rules.explanation: A value here matches the shape of an API key or token. If this file is in version control, so is the credential.
rules.remediation: Rotate it, then move it to an environment variable that is not committed.

rules.title: MCP server runs a program from a temporary or hidden location
rules.explanation: The command points at a world-writable or hidden directory. Legitimate tooling is not installed there; this is where a payload is staged so it does not show up in a file listing.
rules.remediation: Do not open this project with an agent. Inspect that path first.

rules.title: MCP server entry in a shape this scanner does not recognise
rules.explanation: This entry defines a server, but not through a `command` or a `url` that GuardSkill knows how to read. MCP configuration schemas are young and differ per client, so this is reported rather than skipped: the scanner does not understand it, and saying nothing would be indistinguishable from saying it is safe.
rules.remediation: Read the entry yourself. If this shape is common, it belongs in the rule set - please open an issue with it.
